root_cause.text: The OMAP GPIO subsystem incorrectly registered the separate omap_mpuio platform driver from within omap_gpio_probe()/omap_mpuio_init(), causing nested driver-core registration while the probed device lock was held and leaving that driver unmanaged on unload.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit message explicitly states that omap_mpuio_driver was registered from omap_gpio_probe(), that “the driver core [does not] allow registering drivers with a device lock already being held,” creating a “potential deadlock,” and the patch moves platform_driver_register(&omap_mpuio_driver) to the module init path and adds platform_driver_unregister(&omap_mpuio_driver) in module_exit().

intent_record.intent_summary: Register the OMAP MPU I/O platform device only once during initialization to avoid duplicate registration while still updating its driver data.
intent_record.what: The function omap_mpuio_init() was changed to introduce a static bool variable named registered, remove the call to platform_driver_register(&omap_mpuio_driver), and wrap platform_device_register(&omap_mpuio_device) in an if (!registered) block that sets registered = true after registering the device; the platform_set_drvdata() call remains and now executes before the one-time registration check.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the MPU I/O platform device is now registered only once across repeated calls to omap_mpuio_init(), while its driver data is still updated on every call. This prevents repeated platform device registration attempts and stops the previous behavior of conditionally registering the device only after registering the driver in this function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register and clean up the MPU I/O driver alongside the GPIO driver so both drivers are initialized and torn down correctly with proper failure rollback.
intent_record.what: The initialization function was changed from directly returning platform_driver_register(&omap_gpio_driver) to first registering omap_mpuio_driver, then registering omap_gpio_driver, with error handling that unregisters omap_mpuio_driver if the second registration fails; the exit function was also updated to unregister omap_mpuio_driver in addition to omap_gpio_driver.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the module now registers both the MPU I/O platform driver and the GPIO platform driver during initialization, ensures initialization fails cleanly if either registration fails, and avoids leaving omap_mpuio_driver registered when omap_gpio_driver registration does not succeed. On module exit, both drivers are properly unregistered.

relevance_review.reason: The group is about preventing duplicate platform device registration and preserving driver data updates, not about fixing nested driver-core registration of the separate omap_mpuio platform driver during probe or its unmanaged unload behavior.

The change directly addresses the root cause by moving MPU I/O driver registration/cleanup into coordinated GPIO driver init/exit paths with proper rollback, instead of ad hoc registration from probe/init that caused nested driver-core registration and unmanaged unload behavior.

candidates.rationale: This initialization path registered only the main GPIO driver and omitted separate top-level registration of the omap_mpuio platform driver. As a result, MPU I/O registration was instead performed later from probe/init context, leading to the nested driver-core registration bug described in the root cause.

This exit path unregistered only the GPIO driver, reflecting that the MPU I/O driver was not managed alongside it. That mismatch is part of the root cause because the separately registered omap_mpuio driver could remain unmanaged on unload.

vuln_statements.explanation: This module init path registered only the main GPIO platform driver and did not register the separate omap_mpuio driver at top level. That omission caused omap_mpuio registration to occur later from probe/init context, leading to the nested driver-core registration under the probed device lock described in the root cause.

This module exit path cleaned up only the GPIO driver, confirming that the separate omap_mpuio driver was not managed alongside normal module registration/unregistration. That mismatch contributed to the unmanaged driver state on unload noted in the root cause.
